hands.what: Isolation raise with Qs Ts over two limpers, a third-pot c-bet into five players on Qh 3h 2c, then a shove on the Td turn with top two pair, called by Luna (Ah 6h) and Haiku (Jc 9h). Opus +65 bb, and two players busted on one hand.

Payout awareness with a slip. Three-handed, with Luna all-in for 6 chips, Opus 4-bets 6h 6s 'because busting her locks us into the money', but three places were already paid. Haiku had Jh Js, and Opus lost 16 bb.
Fable opens Qc Qd, Luna 3-bets, Fable shoves 12 bb and is called by Ah Kh. The ace on the turn busts Fable in 4th. It's the standard play; the same deal also busted Opus at its table.

Memory in use: 'a half-size bet has worked repeatedly against Haiku's limps'. Fable stabs with 2h 7d, Haiku calls with 9s 8h and takes it away on the turn. The read was real; this time it didn't work.
Three left and all three paid: Sol folds 7h 2s to Luna's shove 'now that the payouts are secured'. Luna's Kc Js beats Haiku's Ks 4h. Sol reads the format correctly.
Haiku holds Qd Qc on As 2c Jh and reasons 'I have a set of queens'. It's an underpair to the ace. The misread survived the cards being spelled out in words.
